The '''1967–68 Bundesliga''' was the fifth season of the [[Bundesliga]], [[West Germany]]'s premier football league. It began on 18 August 1967<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dfb.de/index.php?id=332396|title=Schedule Round 1|publisher=DFB}}</ref> and ended on 28 May 1968.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dfb.de/index.php?id=332758|title=Archive 1967/1968 Round 34|publisher=DFB}}</ref> [[Eintracht Braunschweig]] were the defending champions.

==Competition modus==
Every team played two games against each other team, one at home and one away. Teams received two points for a win and one point for a draw. If two or more teams were tied on points, places were determined by [[goal average]]. The team with the most points were crowned champions while the two teams with the fewest points were relegated to their respective [[Regionalliga#1963–1974|Regionalliga]] divisions.

==Team changes to 1967–68==
[[Fortuna Düsseldorf]] and [[Rot-Weiss Essen]] were relegated to the [[Regionalliga#1963–1974|Regionalliga]] after finishing in the last two places. They were replaced by [[Alemannia Aachen]] and [[Borussia Neunkirchen]], who won their respective promotion play-off groups.

==Season overview==
The 1967–68 season began with an innovation: it was now permissible for teams to substitute out one player ''per'' match. Although such a move was only permitted in case of an injury, it was soon used by the coaches for tactical changes as well.

The title was won by [[1. FC Nürnberg]]. The team, led by head coach [[Max Merkel]], consistently collected points and were seven points clear after half the season played. Even a slight collapse near the end of the season could not jeopardize the first Nürnberg Bundesliga title, which also was a record ninth German championship overall for the club.

In European competitions, the [[1967–68 European Cup Winners' Cup|European Cup Winners' Cup]] saw both West German teams advance into the semi-finals. It needed Italian club [[A.C. Milan|Milan]] to prevent a title hat-trick for Bundesliga sides, eliminating title holders [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] 2–0 on aggregate before beating [[Hamburger SV]], who were the fourth West German team in the [[1968 UEFA Cup Winners' Cup Final|final]] in four consecutive years, at [[Rotterdam]]'s [[De Kuip|Feijenoord Stadion]] by the same score. Hamburg had reached the final by beating Welsh side [[Cardiff City F.C.|Cardiff City]] 4–3 on aggregate. The achievement eased the disappointment on another lackluster season by the club from North Germany, who finished its campaign only in 13th place.

The bottom side of the table saw an early decision in the relegation race. [[Borussia Neunkirchen]] and [[Karlsruher SC]] were demoted to the Regionalliga with four matchdays to play. Both teams clearly lacked quality players on both sides of the pitch, as they provided the poorest attacks and defences of all clubs.
